title: QA Factory — Trapdoor Test
product_promise: A real technically valid video is celebrated by a miniature QA factory, then silently rejected by one human hand and one trapdoor.

beats.entry_visual: The complete cardboard factory and the actual old video playing inside a physical product tile are visible at frame zero.
beats.visual_reason: The real artifact must precede the joke so the rejection feels like honest self-critique rather than a hypothetical skit.
beats.camera_or_motion: A locked top-down camera holds one world while the product tile travels up the center conveyor; three physical QA lamps turn green, a paper PASSED stamp lands, and a few paper scraps celebrate.
beats.asset_provenance: Owned Aaron Studio source master SHA-256 dffda12d3f90e2432c0d451cf2df0574bd2f571b0fcce54387c0b573bccc734c, embedded as the screen texture of a clearly theatrical paper product tile.
beats.sound_cue: Selected Dry Acoustic Deadpan music begins immediately; synthesized scan lands at 0.700s and synthesized stamp at 3.150s.
beats.transition_out: No cut: the same product tile enters the human-review station on the same conveyor axis.
beats.fallback: Image-sequence states at 0.00s and 3.15s preserve the real video tile, three green checks, PASSED stamp, and continuous factory geography.

beats.entry_visual: The product tile remains in the same review bay as the paper human hand enters from above.
beats.visual_reason: A silent human action replaces verbal judgment and creates the awkward pause that makes the trapdoor funny.
beats.camera_or_motion: The paper hand enters on one short ease-out, stops over the product, touches the red reject control, and then holds completely still.
beats.asset_provenance: Built-in image-generation paper-hand asset with local alpha extraction, SHA-256 705bfad22a1b857b041b3375911383d0a16e38973a8c7d3414ead51fb9e6a764; actor prop only, not Aaron's likeness and not evidence.
beats.sound_cue: At 4.600s the music stops at the sample boundary and the synthesized latch clunks; no voice or reaction sound follows.
beats.transition_out: The hand and product hold in the same frame; the unlocked trapdoor becomes the next action without a scene cut.
beats.fallback: A 4.80s still keeps the hand, product tile, red control, and HUMAN REVIEW prop label in the same geography.

beats.entry_visual: The product tile is still centered over the now-unlocked trapdoor while the human hand remains visible.
beats.visual_reason: The physical consequence is the punchline; the viewer should see cause, fall, and result without reading an explanation.
beats.camera_or_motion: The trapdoor rotates 82 degrees on its X hinge using the experimental three-d-flip recipe; the product tile falls on the protected center axis and reveals the physical red NOPE stencil beneath it.
beats.asset_provenance: Deterministic Remotion geometry over the authored factory background; no generated video, simulated UI, or factual claim is introduced.
beats.sound_cue: Digital silence from the opening hinge through the final NOPE hold.
beats.transition_out: Hold the open chute and NOPE stencil through frame 239; no end card or black tail.
beats.fallback: Image-sequence states at 6.20s and 6.75s show the opening door, falling product, and final NOPE state.
